summary: Config guidance: isolate realtime SSE from bulk embed workers to prevent cross-pool token bleed and 429s
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightData Labs is seeing periodic 429s on low-latency SSE streams while a parallel bulk embedding job saturates tenant burst credits. Impact: Intermittent 429s on realtime webhooks and SSE consumers causing degraded product UX during nightly bulk imports. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east running mixed realtime (SSE, webhooks) and bulk embed pipelines under a single tenant config. Observed behaviour: long-lived SSE connections report X-RateLimit-Remaining drifting to zero shortly after a bulk job starts; console shows burst credits consumed rapidly. Customer requests prescriptive configuration to prevent bulk embed work from starving low-latency lanes and guidance for implementing split/priority pools in a dedicated tenant.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On a dedicated tenant, start a sustained SSE connection to /v1/streams with keepalive every 30s.
2) Kick off a high-throughput embedding job that sends 10k small embeds over 20 minutes from the same org key.
3) Observe X-RateLimit-* headers on SSE; monitor console per-route token consumption and tenant burst pool.
4) Note 429s on SSE clients once burst credits drop below threshold and backoff behaviour begins.

2026-03-10 10:03 - Marcus Li: Assigned for triage; will validate rate-limiter logs and pool config. Asked customer for ingestion job manifest and exact API keys used.
2026-03-11 14:40 - BrightData Labs (customer): Provided embedding job concurrency (50 workers), request sizes (avg 300 tokens) and SDK version; confirmed SSE keepalive at 30s and 2s jitter.

investigation_notes: Root hypothesis: Single tenant using default burst pool allows bulk ingest to deplete shared credits; long-lived SSE keepalive heartbeats counted against same pool and appear 'starved'

Observed signed-url callback traffic from embed workers issuing many short POSTs to customer callback endpoint; these callbacks appear in ingress logs and are accounted as interactive tokens rather than background (increases apparent realtime usage)
Console traces: per-route breakdown shows /v1/embed (bulk route) and /v1/streams (realtime route) are both contributing to tenant burst pool; no priority-slicing configured for this tenant
Checked dedicated-pool config: autoscaler healthy, no GPU pressure; issue is quota accounting rather than compute shortage
recommended_config: High-level recommendation: 1) Create isolated burst pools: allocate a dedicated burst pool for realtime (SSE/webhooks) and a separate pool for background bulk ingest. 2) Use route-based priority classes: mark /v1/streams and webhook callback routes as 'low_cost, high-priority' with guaranteed baseline credits. 3) Configure signed-url/callbacks from embed workers to use a background route pattern (path prefix) so they map to the bulk burst pool. 4) Adjust refill intervals: shorter refill for realtime pool (to keep latency-sensitive flows warm) and longer refill for bulk pool with higher capacity. 5) Exempt healthchecks/keepalives from tenant-burst accounting where safe. 6) Add client-side retry jitter and recommended backoff to avoid synchronized retry waves.
resolution: Partial mitigation provided: support gave step-by-step config suggestions and a safe rollout plan. Customer to implement route tagging and separate burst pools in staging; Support will monitor console metrics and re-open if 429s persist post-change.
resolution_notes: Provided JSON config snippet for route -> pool mapping in support response (see below).
Action item: SRE/Platform will add a runbook entry to recommend default split-pool templates for dedicated tenants running mixed realtime+bulk workloads.
Follow-up: instrumented additional telemetry on signed-url callbacks to ensure they map to the intended pool.
next_steps: Customer to apply route tags in staging per recommended_config and report token consumption after next bulk run
Support to validate console metrics (per-route tokens, burst pool remaining) for 48 hours after change
If issue persists, open escalation to RateLimiter team and run controlled repro under support supervision
public_notes: Advised customer that final change requires coordination with tenant admin to avoid service interruption; provided best-practice doc links and example pool templates.
private_notes: Consider adding an automatic detection rule that suggests pool-splitting when a single tenant shows >70% of burst credits consumed by one route for >5 minutes.
Potential product improvement: route-tagging UI in Console to map routes to pools without YAML edits.
